book_meta.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
book_meta.status: public domain — all Holmes entered the US public domain by 2023

sentences.ar: المفتش ليستراد من سكوتلاند يارد كان يزورنا كل شوي بالمسا.
sentences.en: Inspector Lestrade of Scotland Yard visited us every so often in the evening.

sentences.ar: يدخن، ويحكي عن أخبار الشرطة، وهولمز يسمع، ويحفظ.
sentences.en: He smoked, talked of police news, and Holmes listened, and remembered.
And one night, Lestrade said: I have something.

sentences.ar: بس بعتقد إنه شغلك يا دكتور، مش شغل هولمز.
sentences.en: But I think it is your business, doctor, not Holmes's.
Holmes said: illness?
Lestrade said: madness.

sentences.ar: رجل بيكره نابليون لدرجة إنه بيكسر كل تمثال له بيلاقيه.
sentences.en: A man who hates Napoleon so much he breaks every bust of him he finds.

sentences.ar: وحكى: من أربع أيام، واحد فات على محل، وكسر تمثال جبس لنابليون.
sentences.en: And he told: four days ago, a man went into a shop, and smashed a plaster bust of Napoleon.

sentences.ar: وبعدين فات على بيت دكتور، عنده تمثالين.
sentences.en: And then he went into a doctor's house, who had two busts.

sentences.ar: وكسر واحد بالبيت، وأخد التاني وكسره بالحديقة.
sentences.en: And smashed one in the house, and took the other and smashed it in the garden.
Holmes said: the same bust?
Lestrade said: the same copy.

sentences.ar: تلاتة من نفس القالب، من نفس المحل.
sentences.en: Three from the same mould, from the same shop.
Holmes said: and that changes the matter.

sentences.ar: واحد بيكره نابليون بيكسر أي تمثال.
sentences.en: A man who hates Napoleon smashes any bust.
Not three from the same mould.
Lestrade said: meaning?

sentences.ar: قال هولمز: يعني ما بيكره نابليون.
sentences.en: Holmes said: meaning he does not hate Napoleon.
He is looking for something.

sentences.ar: وتاني يوم الصبح، وصل برقية من ليستراد: تعال بسرعة.
sentences.en: And the next morning, a telegram came from Lestrade: come at once.
Kensington.
Murder.

sentences.ar: وبكينسينغتون، صحفي اسمه هاركر، واقف قدام بيته، ووجهه أصفر.
sentences.en: And in Kensington, a journalist named Harker stood before his house, his face pale.
He said: I heard a sound in the night, and went down.

sentences.ar: ولقيت الشباك مفتوح، وتمثال نابليون تبعي راح.
sentences.en: And found the window open, and my Napoleon gone.

sentences.ar: وعالدرج برا، رجل ميت، وحلقه مقطوع.
sentences.en: And on the steps outside, a dead man, his throat cut.

sentences.ar: الميت كان رجل أسمر، طويل، وقوي، وبجيبه صورة.
sentences.en: The dead man was dark, tall and strong, and in his pocket a photograph.

sentences.ar: صورة رجل تاني، وجهه زي القرد، وحواجبه سميكة.
sentences.en: A photograph of another man, with an ape's face, and thick eyebrows.
And with him a knife, an apple, and a string.
Lestrade said: an Italian.
From the Italian quarter.
And Holmes said: and the bust?

sentences.ar: لقوه بعد شارعين، بحديقة بيت فاضي، مكسور لألف قطعة.
sentences.en: They found it two streets away, in the garden of an empty house, smashed into a thousand pieces.

sentences.ar: هولمز رفع كل قطعة، وفحصها، وقال: ما في شي.
sentences.en: Holmes picked up every piece, examined it, and said: nothing.

sentences.ar: وبعدين تطلع بالبيت، وبالشارع، وقال: ليش كسره هون، مش بحديقة هاركر؟
sentences.en: And then he looked at the house, and the street, and said: why did he smash it here, not in Harker's garden?
Lestrade said: he was afraid.
Holmes said: no.
There is light here.
The street lamp.
And Harker's garden is dark.

sentences.ar: كان بده يشوف شو جوا التمثال.
sentences.en: He wanted to see what was inside the bust.
